function: MAPPO agents jointly learn user scheduling, BS active precoding and distributed RIS passive phase shifts to maximize the ergodic sum rate approximation (pp. 6-8)
system: Downlink MU-MISO: BS with M=8 antennas, K=8 single-antenna users (U=2 scheduled), L=2 distributed passive reflecting RISs with N=64 elements each, Rician fading; band not stated (pp. 3, 9)
method: Multi-agent PPO (MAPPO), centralized training with decentralized execution; actor-critic fully connected networks, reinforcement learning with shared reward; BFS-AO solution gives initial observations (pp. 6-8)
data_channel: Self-simulated Rician channels (K=6 dB) with path loss exponents 2.2 and 2.8, statistical CSI; users random in a 6 m circle; 300 channel realizations for evaluation (p. 9)
test_conditions: Trained at Pmax=10 dBm, Rician factor 6 dB, K=8 users; tested at Pmax -5 to 25 dBm, other Rician factors, and fewer users via virtual users (pp. 10-11)
baselines: Non-learned: BFS-AO, BFS-PDS, random precoding, random RIS; learned: BFS-MADDPG (earlier [1]), PPO-MADDPG, PPO-AO, Random-MADDPG (pp. 9-10)
metrics: Ergodic sum rate and its approximation, performance ratio to BFS-AO, Jain fairness index, and running time (pp. 10-13)
complexity: Order O((KM+MUL+NL+C(K,U))I+LI^2) for MAPPO, below BFS-AO and PPO-AO (pp. 8, 12); running time 1.23 ms versus 1957.21 ms for BFS-AO at N=64 (p. 13)
q1_support: p. 3: "Rician fading channel model is adopted. Thus, the channels" are generated by the authors' own simulator with path loss exponents 2.2 and 2.8 (p. 9); no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "trained at Kk,l = 6 dB is tested in other scenarios with" different Rician factors; p. 11: "by adding virtual users with allzero channel matrices" to test fewer users than the K = 8 of training.
q3_support: p. 9: "BFS-AO: Algorithm 1 is proposed to serve as a centralized" non-learned benchmark; p. 10: "in [1] is employed to achieve the link-level optimization" gives the earlier learned MADDPG baseline; p. 1: "6% performance improvement over the state-of-the-art MADRL", on ergodic sum rate (Figs. 7-9).
q4_support: p. 8: "Given a fully connected layer with the input dimension" starts the order of complexity of MAPPO; p. 12: "In Table II, we compare the running time of the above" algorithms, with 1.23 ms for MAPPO against 1957.21 ms for BFS-AO at N = 64 (p. 13).
q5_support: p. 9: "the results, all algorithms are averaged over 300 independent" channel realizations generated by the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 3: the learned agents set the BS precoder and the RIS phase shifts, and the scheduling decision above the physical layer is learned jointly with them, so the work passes the above_phy check. RIS is distributed, passive and reflecting. q2 counts the Rician-factor mismatch and the smaller number of users (Figs. 7b, 8a); the Pmax sweep alone would not count. The abstract claims 6% over state-of-the-art MADRL (p. 1).
